newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia invites more banks to run "S" accounts.
newsitem.headline: Russia invites more banks to run "S" accounts.

text.p: The central bank said on Friday it would allow all banks fulfilling certain conditions to apply for the right to run rouble "S" accounts, through which non-residents can trade on the government securities market.

To apply for the right to run "S" accounts banks must be primary dealers in the market, have a foreign currency licence and have shareholders' funds of at least $30 million rouble equivalent, it said.

Banks already operating "S" accounts which do not fulfil these conditions will lose the right to open new accounts from March 1, 1997, but will be able to continue operating existing accounts, it said.

Since mid-August non-residents have been able to open special rouble "S" accounts at designated Russian banks, and to use funds in these accounts to buy T-bills and government bonds at auctions, and trade in the secondary market.
Non-residents can repatriate funds from these accounts only through forward and option deals with a minimum term of three months.
The mechanism is an important way of attracting foreign investment into Russia. Since it started T-bill yields have fallen sharply.
